title: Integrable envelope for the Gaussian Hessian
statement: Let $I$ be finite, let $v\ge0$ with $v\ne0$, and let $M\ge0$. There is a nonnegative function $b:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ that is integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$ and bounds the operator norm of the product Gaussian density Hessian at every $z\in\mathbb R^I$, uniformly over all $m\in\mathbb R^I$ with $|m_i|\le M$ for every $i\in I$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Put $G_v(c,z)=\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density of variance $v$ for $v>0$ and $p_0=0$, and put $S_v(c,z)[h]=\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$, with division by zero equal to zero. Define $A_v(c,z)[h]=G_v(c,z)S_v(c,z)[h]$ and $T_v(c,z)[h,k]=G_v(c,z)(S_v(c,z)[h]S_v(c,z)[k]-\sum_i h_i k_i/v)$. If $v>0$ and $M\ge0$, there is a nonnegative Lebesgue-integrable $b:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ such that $\|T_v(m,z)\|\le b(z)$ for every $z$ and every $m$ satisfying $|m_i|\le M$ for all $i$; the bilinear operator norm uses maximum norms.
